wording: Peirce characterised truth as the opinion that inquiry would converge on: 'the opinion which is fated to be ultimately agreed to by all who investigate' (1878), later the 'ideal limit towards which endless investigation would tend' (1901); P72 reports the long-standing objection that such epistemic accounts cannot handle 'buried secrets', statements true or false that no inquiry could settle, and Misak's point that we are then never in a position to judge whether a belief is true.
confidence: Moderate as a reading of the SEP entry
counterevidence_limits: Interpretive; pragmatic theories differ widely (James, Dewey, Rorty, Price, Misak) and P72 says there is no consensus response to the fundamental objection. Slip: 'monor functions'.
operationalization: PHI Convergence = Peircean convergence of inquiry
verification_phrases: P72|The opinion which is fated to be ultimately agreed to by all who investigate, is what we mean by the truth || P72|what Peirce called buried secrets
